name: The Shortall household at 1600 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_shortall_john_g

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1600 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1600 John G. Shortall.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1600, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 36, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The one live-in servant it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 is on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. The children the Blue Book lists at the number from 1890 to 1911 are on the card with the years each was listed, whether or not they were at home in 1904. The 1910 census was not read for this card. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: John G. Shortall
persons.note: The 1900 census lists John G. Shortall here as head, born May 1839, in England, came to the United States in 1860, widowed, capitalist (ED 36, sheet 3A, line 17, leaf n669).

persons.name: John L. Shortall
persons.note: Listed at 1600 under John G. Shortall, with his wife, in the 1893 and 1894 editions, and from the 1895 edition next door at 1604, where he and his family live in 1904 on their own card. That he was John G. Shortall's son is read from the shared surname at the number; the Blue Book does not print it.

persons.name: Jessie McKay

born.note: The census gives January 1860, age 40 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Cook" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (cook); born January 1860, in Canada (Eng.), single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.
